decision: The abstract shared-script architecture is expressible; these inspected sources do not yet fix an exact source-grounded common alphabet/normalization/conversion channel. Preserve raw122; do not select a decoder or silently relabel it a tested multilingual-paragraph model.

primary_evidence.title: The first discovery of Judaeo-Syriac: T-S K14.22
primary_evidence.supported: Identifies Syriac medical language written in Jewish Aramaic characters, alphabetical materia medica and occasional Palestinian vowel signs. This is an attributed2013 identification.
primary_evidence.short_quote: a Jewish scribe had transcribed a Syriac medical text
primary_evidence.limit: Only one short source phrase and description; no complete edition or alphabet/conversion table provided here.

primary_evidence.title: A New Judaeo-Syriac Fragment from the Genizah: ENA3846.2
primary_evidence.author: Alan Elbaum
primary_evidence.supported: Opening identifies K14.22 as a trilingual Greek-Aramaic-Middle Persian pharmaceutical lexical list. Footnote4 reports Müller-Kessler’s Eastern Standard Literary Aramaic analysis against Syriac; Elbaum explicitly calls himself a non-expert and favours Syriac. Neither settles the dispute here.
primary_evidence.short_quote: rare trilingual (Greek-Aramaic-Middle Persian) pharmaceutical lexical list
primary_evidence.different_manuscript_caution: The article’s full surviving-text transcription, Hebrew-to-Syriac transliteration and commentary concern ENA3846.2, a fragment of Psalms, not K14.22 or a medical corpus. Reconstruction brackets, merged words, omissions, phonetic spelling, vowel signs and possible copying errors occur. This demonstrates why modern-standard spelling cannot simply be assumed to map letter-for-letter to the historical text.

primary_evidence.title: A Trilingual Pharmaceutical Lexical List: Greek - Aramaic - Middle Persian
primary_evidence.author: Christa Müller-Kessler
primary_evidence.supported: Publisher abstract identifies K14.22 as a ninth-/tenth-century copy of a trilingual plant list in Aramaic square script with sporadic Palestinian vocalization; discusses dialect transfer and Galenic effect grades.
primary_evidence.access: Official abstract retrieved directly. Publisher download returned subscription/login/purchase HTML, not the full article. Full transcription and explicit inventory remain uninspected.

primary_evidence.title: The Judaeo-Syriac Medical Fragment from the Cairo Genizah: A New Edition and Analysis
primary_evidence.author: Siam Bhayro
primary_evidence.supported: Publisher verifies existence and extent of a newer edition; full content requires authentication and was not accessed.

append_only_source_correction_for_root: 122’s historical common-script premise remains supported. K14.22 is specifically a multilingual pharmaceutical lexical list; it does not establish that successive complete paragraphs alternate among different prose languages. Preserve Bhayro2013 as an attributed Syriac identification while recording the published Aramaic classification dispute. Do not treat script identity as phoneme identity or a globally fixed transliteration recipe.
precise_remaining_gaps: Obtain and compare the actual K14.22 editions/transcriptions and apparatus, including Bhayro2017 and Müller-Kessler2017; distinguish preserved signs from editorial reconstruction.

Inventory observed base letters, final shapes, combining/vocalization signs, abbreviations and word boundaries across each candidate medical witness. No such common inventory has been independently established.

Determine whether multilingual content comprises synonym slots/loanwords within single-language entries, complete translated prose, or both. The paragraph-language switch in122 is an analyst hypothesis, not demonstrated by the inspected sources.

If source spelling itself is used as plaintext, define a reversible graphemic cipher separately from historical language-to-script conversion; the latter may involve many-to-one phonetic changes and cannot be inferred from the common alphabet alone.
possible_research_direction_not_selected: The stronger specific source observation may motivate a #13 self-defining multilingual dictionary together with #44 shared-script channel, but complete entry compilation, language slots and joint identity constraints need their own source contract. No new proposal or gate claim made here.
exposure: No Voynich data/images, corpus construction or decoder implementation. Original122proposal/registry not modified. PDFs are official archived webpages, not the copyrighted full editions.
